about:
Missouri Basin Materials operates from Bismarck, North Dakota, serving as a concrete material supplier across the Upper Midwest. The company provides a full range of products and services for concrete construction, from rebar fabrication to anchor bolts and safety equipment.

The business fabricates rebar and prepares shop drawings with an emphasis on quick turnaround, and it supplies a broad lineup of concrete accessories including void forms, corrugated paper products, plumbing drainage items, and forming products from vendors such as Five Star, Newark Paperboard, Paragon, and Polyguard. An in-house estimating department prepares quotes for projects and upcoming bids.

Missouri Basin Materials serves contractors and project owners in commercial, industrial, and infrastructure construction. Its project history includes ring wall foundations and water treatment plants across North Dakota, Montana, Wyoming, South Dakota, and surrounding states.

The company highlights its rapid rebar fabrication and shop drawing response, along with dedicated estimating support, as key differentiators that help customers meet bid deadlines and project schedules.

old_description: Mitas Electronics combines miniature high-speed interconnect experience, precision manufacturing discipline, and future-facing transport architecture work to support more predictable physical data movement as systems scale.
about:
Mitas Electronics is headquartered in Round Rock, Texas. The company has accumulated over 17 years of operating history, though a specific founding year has not been disclosed. Ownership structure and founder names are not publicly shared.

The company specializes in miniature high-speed interconnect systems, offering disciplined interconnect engineering, cable assembly design, manufacturing coordination, and technical support. Its service portfolio includes application review, mechanical fit analysis, signal-path and channel physics analysis, DFMA guidance, supply chain management, process documentation, and repeatable execution across manufacturing partners. Mitas also maintains a library of technical binders covering connector families such as QSFP-DD, CABLINE-CA II, and CABLINE-VS II. To date, the company reports more than 4 million cables shipped, over 500 customers served, and 2,200 tailored solutions delivered.

Mitas serves engineering teams working on high-speed data transport and demanding electronic systems, particularly in environments where mechanical execution, electrical behavior, and validation planning affect reliable data movement. Its customer base includes organizations developing next-generation computing architectures and data-center infrastructure, though specific industry verticals are not enumerated publicly.

The company positions itself as an engineering-led organization with manufacturing depth, emphasizing a future-facing data transport direction through its GFx™ architecture and technical binder systems. Quality is framed as an engineering discipline, with defined inspection steps, traceability practices, and continual improvement loops intended to make interconnect outcomes more predictable.

name: Mitchell Furniture Systems Inc
old_description: As an innovator in wall mounted table and bench systems since the early 1950’s, Mitchell offers value without compromising its pledge for a safe and secure product that will provide decades of service.
about:
Mitchell Furniture Systems traces its roots to Milwaukee, Wisconsin, where William Mitchell founded the company in 1896 to produce dairy-farm equipment such as automatic stalls, pens, and stanchions. Over the next decades the firm expanded its metal-fabricating expertise into park and playground steel products sold nationwide.

Today Mitchell operates plants in Fredonia and Milwaukee, where seasoned fabricators and assemblers combine time-honored metalworking with robotic welding to build the company's full line of tables and seating. The product range includes wall-mounted table-and-bench systems (a category Mitchell pioneered in the early 1950s), mobile PorTables with integrated seating, Fold-N-Roll folding tables, 3-in-1 ConverTables that convert cafeteria space to theater or lecture configurations, Saturna adjustable-height and Fold-O-Leg folding tables, and choral risers. Steel frames paired with wood tops remain the core construction method, and the company also offers a top-replacement service for both its own tables and competitors' units.

Primary customers are K–12 school districts, municipalities, churches, and commercial offices that need durable cafeteria, classroom, fellowship-hall, conference-room, and lecture-hall furniture. Mitchell's risers have served educational and municipal facilities since the late 1940s, and many early installations remain in service.

The company emphasizes "Made in America By Mitchell" as its differentiator, citing domestic production, robotic welding precision, and a design philosophy aimed at decades-long product life. Immediate delivery is advertised for stocked items.

name: Mitsubishi Electric US, Inc., Industrial Automation
old_description: Mitsubishi Electric US, Industrial Automation announces the launch of the GOT3000 Series HMI, the next generation of human-machine interfaces, to its existing lineup. GOT3000 delivers faster performance, enhanced security, and compatibility with prior GOT models. It delivers a practical path to modernization without the need for rip-and-replace upgrades.
about:
Mitsubishi Electric US, Inc., Industrial Automation operates from a facility in Vernon Hills, Illinois, serving as the Americas hub for the Japanese conglomerate's factory automation business. The parent company, Mitsubishi Electric Corporation, marked its 100th anniversary in February 2021, with the factory automation division representing a substantial portion of that legacy. The U.S. division was established to consolidate sales, marketing, service, engineering, and manufacturing resources under one roof.

The division designs and manufactures a broad portfolio of industrial automation equipment, including programmable logic controllers (MELSEC iQ-R, iQ-F, Q, L, and F series), human-machine interfaces (GOT3000 series), variable frequency drives (FREQROL FR-D800 series), AC servo systems (MELSERVO), industrial robots (MELFA), collaborative robots (ASSISTA), computerized numerical controllers, laser processing machines, and electrical discharge machines. The Vernon Hills campus integrates manufacturing, engineering, training, customer service, repair, sales, and warehousing functions, enabling end-to-end support for automation deployments.

Customers span mining, water and wastewater treatment, automotive, and education sectors. Documented projects include a comprehensive automation solution for mining safety and material handling with DICISA, a municipal lift station pump upgrade for energy efficiency with Bertelkamp Automation, robotic machine tending for e-motor production at Renault Group, and hands-on automation technology programs at Kettering University. The company also supports a network of Diamond Partner distributors, solutions providers, and OEMs, as well as system integrators through its Solutions Partner program.

The division's stated mission is to support the industrial automation needs of customers in the Americas through combined resources and a culture of continuous improvement (Kaizen). Mitsubishi Electric ranks among the top five global filers of international patent applications, and the company emphasizes product security through dedicated vulnerability management initiatives. Quality management systems underpin its commitment to meeting or exceeding customer expectations, while rapid repair turnaround using custom parts and on-site training aim to minimize downtime.

name: Mobile Electronics Inc

about:
Mobile Electronics Inc was founded in 1979 in Huntsville, Alabama, as a small business specializing in the distribution of electronic connectors. The company operates from a facility on Poole Drive and holds ISO 9001:2015 certification.

The firm focuses on circular connectors for aerospace, defense, and medical applications, maintaining an extensive in-stock inventory of military and commercial backshell products. Its Huntsville warehouse supports same-day shipping for many items and next-day availability for most needs. Value-added services include connector inspection, counterfeit prevention, and technical consultation backed by a sales team with over 100 years of combined connector experience.

Primary customers operate in the avionics, aerospace, defense, and medical sectors, ranging from large manufacturing firms to global clients. The distributor's approach emphasizes listening to project requirements and advising on optimal connector solutions rather than simply fulfilling part-number orders.

The company's stated mission highlights the versatility and flexibility afforded by its small-business size, combined with deep product knowledge, positioning it as a circular connector source in the United States. All products are warranted and ship with certification.

name: Modular Components National
old_description: Modular Components National is a manufacturer of printed microwave circuit boards.
about:
Modular Components National (MCN) operates from Forest Hill, Maryland, where it was founded in 1981. The privately held company manufactures printed microwave circuit boards for government and commercial RF customers.

MCN specializes in the fabrication of RF and microwave printed circuitry, with a focus on PTFE substrates. Its capabilities include single- and double-sided circuits, mixed-dielectric and PTFE multilayers, metal-backed constructions, and fusion bonding. The shop offers laser routing for thin dielectrics, wire-bondable gold finishes, embedded copper heat-sink cores, and thermoclastic bond films such as FEP lamination. Materials processed include laminates from Arlon, Rogers, and Taconic, as well as FR-4 and other microwave laminates.

The company serves the defense, aerospace, telecommunications, and medical markets, supplying both government agencies and commercial RF customers. Its sales network covers the United States, Canada, and Israel through independent representatives.

It also provides design guides and comparison sheets to assist customers with material selection and board construction.
